claim.statement: An explicitly compiled fresh-process Darwin probe runs one pinned hidden-1024 DINOv3 embedding projection at 512x512 on the CPU reference path with an exact 805306368-MAC budget, finite outputs, and a 512 MiB RSS watchdog.
claim.scope: One user-local safetensors artifact, four embedding roles, one 512px CPU forward, and post-GC/process-resident orientation only; no true peak, native allocator, transformer block, full encoder, GPU, or Metal claim.

evidence.result: rejects before payload/forward work because the production 67108864-MAC limit is below 805306368

dod: The model-scale API is compiled only with dinov3_model_scale_forward_probe; default forward keeps MAX_MULTIPLY_ADDS at 67108864.
The probe requires an explicit checkpoint path, exact pinned MAC budget, and positive RSS watchdog limit.
The pinned file size, four-role F32 byte count, role digest, output shapes/bytes, and finite output are checked.
The probe reports load/forward allocation and post-GC/RSS orientations while marking true peak, native memory, blocks, and Metal explicitly unmeasured or unrun.
No-codegen build, focused flagged spec, default DINOv3 suite, and CPU-only production compile pass.

excluded: default production multiply-add or RSS policy widening

residual_risks: The RSS watchdog is a process-resident safety cap, not a true high-water or native allocator certificate.
Post-GC managed-heap and RSS deltas are local orientation signals and can vary with runtime roots, allocator state, and host noise.
The forward uses a zero-filled CPU input and establishes finiteness/shape/guard behavior, not numerical parity against Python/Transformers or image quality.
The 24 transformer blocks, final normalization, decoder, GPU, and Metal remain unimplemented or unrun.
The one fixed-artifact run does not establish production latency, concurrency, or a safe 1024px budget.
